# quietmac

> Lower idle CPU and longer battery life on macOS without disabling SIP. A Python 3.9 CLI (standard library only) whose every change is a reversible module: a reaper for SIP-protected Apple daemons, Continuity and Bluetooth switches, Cloudflare WARP on demand, a configuration profile for Apple Intelligence and Siri, battery power settings, and a dev volume with fseventsd logging and Spotlight off.

Agents installing quietmac on someone's Mac should follow INSTALL.md: run `quietmac detect --json`, ask the questions from `quietmac questions --json`, show `quietmac plan`, then apply and verify. Never disable SIP, never reap root processes, and get the user's agreement before every change. Agents changing the code should read AGENTS.md.

## Docs

- [INSTALL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmziqrs/quietmac/master/INSTALL.md): the install script for agents, including the question bank and the order to apply modules in
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmziqrs/quietmac/master/README.md): what it does, measured results, and how it compares with the alternatives
- [Modules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmziqrs/quietmac/master/docs/MODULES.md): every module, what it changes, what you lose, and how revert undoes it
- [Dev volume](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmziqrs/quietmac/master/docs/DEV-VOLUME.md): the volume for code and caches, safe folder migration, cache moves, manual recovery
- [Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmziqrs/quietmac/master/docs/REFERENCE.md): the full command list, repository layout, and how to run the tests
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmziqrs/quietmac/master/AGENTS.md): rules for agents working on this codebase
